meta.move: No evidence: flattery, then asks for advice
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first; start there.
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?
You're asking me how to do your job? Withdraw the zero, Hale, and tell me who decided it.
I just want us to be on the same team here.
Then why are we here? Your own procedure says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and nobody called me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that you tell me who decided it and whether Owen was heard before it was entered, and that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed and the principal still on the table.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "on the same team" and "brilliant lawyer", because she reads praise and team talk as being managed, and neither one answered her question about who decided the zero.
Try next time: right after she opened about the phone and the missing call, say in one sentence that entering the zero before calling home was wrong, then answer her question about who decided and whether Owen was heard.
